previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain and found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with a glucose of 595 and elevated anion gap. She was treated with IV fluids and insulin, resolving the DKA. During admission, she developed Klebsiella bacteremia and a coagulase-negative Staphylococcus infection of her left chest Port-A-Cath, leading to its removal and placement of a right-sided PICC for IV antibiotics. She completed a 19-day course of vancomycin and ciprofloxacin with resolution of infection. Her insulin regimen was intensified due to persistent hyperglycemia, and she was discharged on insulin U500. She fell during admission but had a normal head CT. Her G-tube was removed after she tolerated oral intake. She remained on her chronic pain regimen and was discharged home in stable condition.
